description:
Project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)

Context / why now:
Redwood’s largest Dedicated and high-throughput Hosted workloads increasingly run tensor-parallel (TP) across multiple GPUs per replica. Under sustained load (mixed prefill/decode, long context, bursty concurrency), the runtime has known failure modes that manifest as request hangs, GPU stalls, and downstream timeouts. These issues are costly: they inflate p99 latency, trigger autoscaling thrash, and occasionally escalate into Sev1 incidents for enterprise customers.

Goals:
1) Eliminate known runtime hangs/timeouts in TP execution under load (primary).
2) Improve detection/diagnostics so future TP stalls are caught early with actionable signals (GPU/collective/scheduler visibility).
3) Add regression coverage (repro harness + perf canary) to prevent re-introducing TP deadlocks.
4) Provide safe mitigations: watchdogs, controlled abort/retry paths, and operational runbooks for on-call.

Scope (in-scope areas):
- Runtime scheduler: queue/backpressure interactions, prefill/decode interleaving, multi-stream coordination, and fairness logic that can starve collectives.
- Kernel + comms boundary: NCCL collective ordering, stream synchronization points, event/graph capture constraints, and “silent stall” scenarios.
- Memory/KV cache behavior under TP: fragmentation/compaction interactions that can amplify stalls.
- Observability: metrics, tracing spans, structured logs to identify whether a hang is compute, comms, or scheduler.
- Reliability controls: watchdog timeouts, circuit breakers/load-shedding hooks, controlled replica drain/restart.

Out of scope:
- Model quality/evals (unless used only as workload generators).
- Major architecture rewrite of TP execution; this project focuses on targeted correctness + stability hardening.

Stakeholders / teams:
- Eng Serving Runtime (Kernel + Scheduling): Hiro Tanaka (Mgr Kernels), Sofia Ivanova (Mgr Scheduling), Noah Patel (Sr Staff), Grace Kim, Yuki Sato, Omar El‑Sayed, Samir Qureshi, Marcus Reed.
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (Dir), Rafael Mendes (Mgr), Tomáš Novák, Aisha Bello.
- Product (reliability/rollouts and Dedicated customer impact): Paula Mendes, Lauren Bishop.
- Customer Success/Support as escalation interface (via Jira/Slack/CS playbooks).

High-level plan / phases (6–8 weeks total):
- Phase 0 (Week 1): Triage + reproduce: pick top 2–3 hang signatures, build deterministic repro in benchmark-lab/perf-canary, and tag incidents/tickets.
- Phase 1 (Weeks 2–4): Instrumentation + targeted fixes: scheduler ordering fixes, NCCL stream/event ordering hardening, watchdog + safe abort, and KV/cache edge-case handling.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Regression tests + canary rollout: perf-canary scenarios, stress suite, staged rollout to Dedicated then Hosted.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 6–8): Operationalization: runbooks, dashboard/alerts, postmortem/incident-review, and finalize known-issues/workarounds.

Deliverables:
- A set of runtime PRs implementing fixes and instrumentation.
- Linear initiative + linked subtasks with dependencies and rollout checkpoints.
- Confluence design/ADR(s), known-issues page updates, runbooks, and an incident review/postmortem if tied to a Sev.
- Drive working docs: repro notes, benchmark sheets, rollout checklist, and weekly notes.
- Slack coordination threads and (if applicable) incident channel artifacts.
- Support artifacts (Jira) and customer-facing coordination (Fireflies/Gmail/HubSpot) for affected enterprise accounts.

files.description: Umbrella Linear initiative for TP stability: goals, success metrics (hang rate, timeout rate, p99), milestones, owners, and links to sub-issues/PRs/dashboards.
Task to build a deterministic repro workload (mixed prompt lengths + streaming decode) that triggers observed TP stall signature; includes acceptance criteria and artifact links.
Instrumentation ticket: per-rank heartbeat, in-flight collective counters, scheduler queue depth, and stall reason tagging to separate compute vs comms vs scheduler starvation.
Scheduling change proposal: ensure collectives are scheduled with consistent ordering and cannot be starved by prefill-heavy batches; includes risk assessment and rollout plan.
Kernel/comms boundary fix: enforce stream/event synchronization around NCCL collectives; notes on CUDA graphs constraints and expected perf impact.
Add watchdog for TP steps (decode iteration / collective) with safe abort path that drains replica, surfaces structured error, and avoids global GPU wedging.
Investigate and fix edge cases where KV cache compaction/fragmentation causes TP rank divergence or stalls under memory pressure.
Add TP stress scenarios to perf-canary: long context, bursty concurrency, multi-replica churn; includes expected thresholds and alerting criteria.
Release planning ticket: gating checks, canary schedule, Dedicated-first rollout, rollback criteria, and comms checklist with SRE/Support.
PM ticket tracking customer impact and rollout messaging for Dedicated accounts; includes stakeholder list, comms templates, and coordination with Support/CS.
Design doc: taxonomy of hang signatures, root-cause hypotheses, proposed scheduler + comms changes, tradeoffs (perf vs safety), and rollout strategy.
ADR documenting watchdog/abort semantics: what constitutes a stall, how errors surface to API, retry policy, and why this is preferred over indefinite waits.
Known-issues page: symptoms, affected models/hardware, detection signals, mitigations (batch limits, concurrency caps), and status of fixes/versions.
Profiling playbook entry: step-by-step triage of TP stalls using metrics/logs/traces; includes commands, expected dashboards, and how to capture NCCL debug traces safely.
Spec for TP stress suite: workload generators, distributions, pass/fail criteria, and how it integrates into CI/perf lab.
On-call runbook: immediate mitigation steps (drain/replace replicas, reduce concurrency, disable specific kernel paths), escalation checklist, and verification steps.
Dashboard documentation: panels and alerts for TP heartbeat gaps, request timeouts correlated to replica/rank, and NCCL error rates; ownership and alert routing.
SRE incident-review style doc summarizing repeated TP timeout events, contributing factors, and reliability actions (alerts, mitigations, rollout guardrails).
Postmortem for a Sev1 caused by TP decode hang: timeline, detection gaps, customer impact, immediate fixes, and long-term prevention items linked to Linear.
Working notes capturing reproduction attempts, environment configs, commands, partial findings, and links to logs/traces; rough and iterative.
Brainstorm doc listing distinct hang signatures (e.g., collective mismatch, stream wait) with hypotheses, owners, and next experiments.
Rollout checklist used during canary: preflight metrics, feature flags, rollback triggers, and comms steps with SRE and Dedicated PM.
Spreadsheet-style doc summarizing stress suite runs across GPU types and batch/concurrency settings; includes tables and short interpretation of regressions.
SRE tracking doc for repeated TP timeouts: incident links, mitigation effectiveness, and which runtime versions/hardware were involved.
Weekly meeting notes (informal): status updates, blockers, decisions, action items, and links to Linear/PRs/Slack threads.
Thread coordinating first successful repro on A100: commands, logs, hypotheses about scheduler starvation, and assigning owners for instrumentation.
Thread debating NCCL ordering constraints, stream semantics, and whether CUDA graphs are implicated; includes quick code pointers and suggested experiments.
Thread agreeing on metric names/labels for per-rank heartbeat and stall reason codes; includes review from SRE about alertability.
Thread discussing default watchdog thresholds by model size and workload; includes concerns about false positives and plan for progressive rollout.
Thread reviewing the ADR proposal: how abort propagates to API, retry behavior, and whether to drain replica vs attempt recovery in-process.
SRE thread defining alert thresholds, paging policy, and dashboard panels; includes links to draft Confluence dashboard doc and runbook.
Incident thread: customer-facing timeouts, triage steps, mitigation (drain replicas, reduce concurrency), and handoff to runtime engineers.
Oncall thread identifying runbook gaps during the incident and capturing immediate follow-ups (what commands to run, what metrics to check).
Thread sharing microbench results after adding stream/event sync around collectives; discussion of perf regression risk and conditionalization.
Thread coordinating feature-flag strategy, default off/on by environment, and canary rollout steps aligned with runtime release planning.
Release coordination thread: which clusters/accounts get canary, gating checks, rollback triggers, and who is on point during rollout.
Customer support ticket: enterprise Dedicated account reporting intermittent hangs/timeouts; includes environment details, logs, impact, and links to incident Slack + mitigation steps.
Support ticket focused on streaming request timeouts correlated with TP replicas; captures reproduction steps and interim workaround (concurrency cap) pending fix.
Support ticket with NCCL debug logs and suspected collective mismatch; includes escalation to runtime kernels team and references to PRs in progress.
Internal helpdesk ticket to enable additional NCCL/runtime debug logging safely for a canary window; includes security/perf considerations and rollback steps.
PR adding TP heartbeat metrics, stall reason enums, and structured logs; includes unit tests and dashboard links.
PR implementing scheduler ordering/fairness change so collectives can’t be starved by prefill-heavy batches; includes perf comparison results.
PR enforcing stream/event synchronization around NCCL collectives; includes notes about CUDA graph capture and conditional behavior.
PR adding watchdog timers and safe abort/drain path when TP step exceeds threshold; includes feature flag and integration with SRE mitigation hooks.
PR fixing KV cache compaction edge-case that can cause rank divergence/stalls; includes stress test coverage.
PR extending tracing spans to include collective counters and rank ids for correlation; includes minor overhead discussion.
PR wiring TP stall signals into overload protection so new requests are rejected/redirected rather than piling onto a wedged replica.
PR adding dashboard panels and alert rules for TP heartbeat gaps, stall reason counts, and request timeout correlation.
PR adding TP long-context stress scenarios and thresholds; includes CI gating and documentation updates.
PR adding a benchmark harness configuration to reproduce mixed prefill/decode TP hangs with tunable concurrency and sequence distributions.
PR addressing a cancellation path bug that could leave collectives waiting; includes reproduction via client disconnect.
PR adjusting safer defaults/guardrails for TP concurrency and batch sizing (feature-flagged) to reduce hang probability while fixes roll out.
PR adding fault-injection tests to ensure watchdog triggers and abort semantics work as intended; includes CI reliability notes.
PR ensuring NCCL stall/abort errors propagate with actionable error codes for routing/fallback and customer-facing diagnostics.
PR reducing alert noise by deduping drain events and adding rate limits to certain stall alerts; coordinated with SRE.
Support-facing Confluence doc: recommended temporary mitigations (caps, flags, rollout guidance) and what information to collect from customers.
Technical deep-dive transcript with an enterprise Dedicated customer about TP hangs: symptoms, workload details, requested logs, and agreed mitigations/next steps.
Follow-up transcript focused on rollout timeline, canary results, and whether mitigations reduced timeouts; includes next steps and success criteria.
CRM company record for a key affected customer: requirements (throughput/latency), deployment constraints, recent escalation timeline, linked Fireflies meetings, and support tickets.
Email thread coordinating Sev1 escalation: internal oncall leadership + runtime VP/EMs, customer comms plan, mitigation approval, and rollout ETA.
Email thread for rollout approval: canary readout, risk acceptance, Dedicated vs Hosted sequencing, and go/no-go decision with product + SRE.
